items.title: Jon-Erik Kellso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I had done maybe a half dozen gigs with Milt Hinton... I called him up... he did it and I was thrilled. And he was a great help and a great inspiration in the studio.

ctx.x: That must have been a good experience.

Oh, boy, yeah. Well he was the highlight of that session for me, which was full of great musical moments and playing with great guys. Again, they were all top-notch guys. Mat Domber of Arbors Records was great because he asked me to do this CD after having done a few as a sideman for him. And of course that was a great thrill and honor. But also he really left it in my hands to pick the guys and the tunes and the studio and the engineer, and so I really got to do it my own way and write some original tunes and…

because he’s always liked to help out and encourage younger players who he felt were on the right track or trying to keep the music going and all of that. So he did it and I was thrilled. And he was a great help and a great inspiration in the studio. There was times when I would start to count off a tune and I’d think wait a second, I should ask Milt to count this tune off. Because he was on like the original recording of it and has played it with all the best bands in history. And if anybody knows what tempo…
